title: Are people drinking less alcohol?
description_html:
In recent generations many people have chosen to stop drinking alcohol. Surveys from the UK suggest that 16 to 24-year-olds are more likely to be non-drinkers than the older generations. Many people are sharing their experience of drinking less alcohol or being completely sober on social media. Some people have been saying that they want to go out more to drink and have fun with friends, but they have concerns about fitness and wellness. Georgie and Neil discuss this and teach you some new vocabulary.

6 Minute English now has a VIDEO VERSION! 6 Minute English now comes with a video! It's the same programme that you know and love, but now you can see us! Watch this podcast here (and find a free worksheet):

https://www.bbc.co.uk/learningenglish/english/features/6-minute-english_2026/ep-261008 Let us know what you think of the new version of 6 Minute English at learningenglish@bbc.co.uk

cues.t: Hi Neil.
Hi Georgie.
Do you want to hear something quite unusual for me?
Err, yes!
I haven't had an alcoholic drink this year.
Wow!
That is really impressive.
How do you feel?
Like a new person?
I do feel very good, I have to say.
I can't say the same – I did have a few alcoholic drinks at the weekend with my friends.
But in many parts of the world, people don't drink alcohol at all.
In the UK it's very common – that is until recently.
Today on 6 Minute English, we're going to find out why many people are choosing to give up or cut down on alcohol, and we'll be asking, "Is this the end of British drinking culture?"
OK.
Neil, let's start with a quiz question.
Many people in the UK and other countries choose to give up alcohol in the new year for the whole of the month of January, but what is the challenge called?
Is it: a) No-drink New Year b) Alcohol-free January, or c) Dry January?
Well, I know the answer to this, but I'm not going to give it away.
OK.
Well, then our listeners can find out the answer at the end of the programme.
Yes, they can.
So, Georgie, I hear all the time that younger people don't drink as much alcohol today as they used to in the past.
Is that true?
Well, in the UK, surveys suggest that 16 to 24-year-olds are more likely to be non-drinkers than the older generations.
OK.
So, why are more young people choosing to be sober?
That means not to drink alcohol.
Well, the BBC World Service podcast What in the World have been investigating this.
Presenter Hannah Gelbart met three young people who choose to be sober for some alcohol-free drinks to find out more.
Here's Daniel's story:
Yeah.
So, today I don't drink at all, but when I was in my early 20s, I think I felt maybe a bit of, like, societal pressure – you know, work drinks or being at uni, where it was the norm to just join in.

I think you'd probably get a few weird glances if you're like, "Yeah, I'm not going to join in at all." So, I did that and I think Covid lockdown just gave me a bit of confidence to say, "OK, let me step away from this.
It's not necessarily something I want to do moving forward."
So, how many years have you been sober for?
I would say it's been six years now.
Six years?
So, Daniel says that when he was younger, he felt societal pressure to drink alcohol.
Societal pressure is feeling like you need to do something because lots of people around you are doing it.
Right.
So, Daniel says drinking was the norm at university and after work.
The norm is a way of saying that something is normal or common.
But during the Covid-19 pandemic, when people in the UK were unable to socialise and visit pubs and bars, Daniel's attitude to alcohol changed.
After that, he decided to be sober and he hasn't had a drink for about six years.
So, Georgie, it seems like many young people don't drink at all and lots of them share their experience of being sober on social media.
But recently there's been a bit of a change, hasn't there?
Yes.

Whilst many people use social media to share their experience of drinking less alcohol or no alcohol at all, some people have been saying that they want to go out more and drink and have fun with friends.
They argue we're too worried about fitness and wellness, and that drinking some alcohol to have a good time is fine.
Here's Millie talking more about this to BBC World Service podcast What in the World:
I think we had this, like, rise of self-optimisation content.
I think unfortunately sobriety, kind of, got swept in with that and it got touted as this way to, you know, get up at 5am, do a HYROX.
And, you know, for many of us, that's probably not our reality with not drinking.
It's that we do it to feel a bit more sane or, you know, things like that.
And so, I think now we are entering this, like, almost pushback era of that content and you're seeing celebrities...
Like, it's not just alcohol – you're seeing more celebrities smoking and, like, posting that on their Instagram and not worrying if it's brand-friendly.
OK.
So, Millie thinks that being sober is associated with certain kinds of self-optimisation content, where people talk about fitness, diet and having big goals for themselves.
Yes, and Millie says being sober gets touted as a way to get up at 5am to exercise.
In other words, people talk about it a lot and try to encourage people to do it.
But Millie says that being sober isn't always about being super fit and healthy.
For her, it's about being sane.
But still, Millie thinks there's a pushback against self-optimisation content.
Pushback means a criticism of the content, and people are pushing back by doing the opposite.
For example, lots of celebrities post about themselves drinking and smoking.
Well, Georgie, I've decided to try to give up alcohol for a whole year, but I don't think everybody should do that if they don't want to.
It's really up to the individual.
Yeah, I still enjoy having a few drinks with my friends.
I think it's just all about balance, really. OK.
Neil, it's time to reveal the answer to this week's question.
I asked, "What was the name given for when people give up alcohol in January?"
Yes.
And the answer is Dry January.
That is correct. Well done!
Let's recap the vocabulary we learned in this programme, starting with sober, which describes someone who doesn't drink alcohol or take recreational drugs.
Societal pressure is the feeling that you should do something because lots of other people expect you to.
Saying something is the norm is a way to say it's usual or common.
Self-optimisation content means videos and posts about being fit, healthy and achieving big goals.
If somebody touts an idea or lifestyle, they talk about it a lot and try to convince people to do it.
And pushback is strong criticism of a trend, and people doing the opposite.
Once again, our six minutes are up, but don't forget to test what you've learned with the worksheet on our website, bbclearningenglish.com.
Thank you for joining us and goodbye.
Goodbye!

study.one_liner_ko: 영국 등에서 젊은 층을 중심으로 금주·절주가 늘어난 이유와, 이에 대한 반작용(pushback)까지 짧게 훑는 에피소드.
summary_ko: 진행자 닐은 올해 술을 한 잔도 마시지 않았다고 말하며 시작한다. 영국의 술 문화가 정말 끝나가는지가 이번 주제다.
영국 조사에 따르면 16~24세는 윗세대보다 술을 안 마시는 비율이 높다. 대니얼은 20대 초반에 직장 회식과 대학 분위기 때문에 사회적 압력을 느꼈다고 한다. 코로나 봉쇄 때 거리를 둘 자신감이 생겨 6년째 술을 끊었다.
SNS에는 금주 경험담이 많다. 그런데 최근에는 친구들과 나가서 즐겁게 마시고 싶다는 목소리도 나온다. 건강과 웰빙에 너무 집착한다는 주장이다.
밀리는 금주가 새벽 5시 기상, 운동 같은 자기계발 콘텐츠와 한데 묶여 홍보됐다고 본다. 자신에게 금주는 정신적으로 덜 지치려는 선택이라고 말한다. 지금은 그런 콘텐츠에 대한 반발(pushback)의 시대로 들어서고 있고, 유명인이 흡연 사진을 올리는 것도 그 예다.
닐은 1년 금주를 시도하지만 선택은 개인 몫이라고 한다. 조지는 적당한 균형이 중요하다고 말한다. 퀴즈 정답은 Dry January였고, 마지막에 sober, societal pressure, the norm, self-optimisation content, tout, pushback을 복습한다.
study.summary_en: This week's episode asks whether British drinking culture is on its way out. Surveys suggest that 16 to 24-year-olds are more likely to be non-drinkers than older generations. One guest said he felt real societal pressure to drink in his early twenties, and lockdown gave him the confidence to step away from it. But there's now a bit of pushback against sober content that gets touted as part of a perfect fitness routine. Some people just want to go out and enjoy a drink with friends. The hosts' take is pretty balanced: it's up to the individual, and it's all about balance.

chapters.title_en: Neil's alcohol-free year and the big question
Quiz: what is the January challenge called?
Why young people choose to be sober
The pushback against sober self-optimisation content
It's up to the individual, answer and vocab recap
chapters.title_ko: 개인의 선택, 정답 공개, 어휘 복습

expressions.quote: I'm not going to give it away
expressions.nuance_ko: 답이나 반전, 결말을 일부러 말하지 않을 때 쓴다. give the game away, give away the ending 형태로도 자주 쓰인다. 장난스럽고 가벼운 구어체다.
examples: I know who's getting promoted, but I'm not going to give it away.
Don't give away the ending! I haven't finished the series yet.
Her smile gave it away. She'd obviously already heard the news.

similar.example: Come on, spill the beans. Where are you going on holiday?
He let it slip that the launch is delayed.

expressions.quote: choosing to give up or cut down on alcohol
expressions.nuance_ko: give up(완전히 끊다)과 대비해 쓰는 것이 핵심이다. 습관, 소비, 지출 등을 점진적으로 줄일 때 널리 쓴다. 대화에서 자연스럽고 격식 있는 자리에서도 무난하다.
examples: I'm trying to cut down on coffee, but it's hard with this schedule.
We need to cut down on meetings. Half of them could be emails.
He's cut down on eating out since the prices went up.

similar.example: They had to scale back their holiday plans.
I'm easing off sugar rather than quitting completely.

expressions.quote: let me step away from this.
expressions.nuance_ko: 물리적으로 떠나는 것이 아니라, 습관·논쟁·역할에서 의식적으로 물러난다는 뜻이다. 부드럽고 성숙한 느낌을 준다. 'I need to step away from the news for a while.'처럼 쓴다.
examples: I had to step away from social media for a month. It was draining me.
Let's step away from the spreadsheet for a second and talk about the bigger picture.
After the argument, she stepped away from the group chat.

similar.example: Let's take a step back and look at what we actually want.
He tried to distance himself from the rumours.

expressions.quote: drinking was the norm at university and after work
expressions.meaning_ko: 표준, 보통 있는 일, 통상적인 관행
expressions.nuance_ko: be the norm, become the norm, the new norm 형태로 많이 쓴다. 'It's quite normal'보다 사회적·집단적 관행이라는 느낌이 강하다. 토론에서 '요즘은 이게 기본값이다'를 말할 때 유용하다.
examples: In my last office, working late was the norm.
Remote work has become the norm for a lot of people in my field.
Tipping is the norm in the US, but it isn't in Japan.

similar.example: Background checks are standard practice here.
Delays are par for the course on that airline.

expressions.quote: he felt societal pressure to drink alcohol
expressions.nuance_ko: 주변 사람들의 기대나 분위기가 개인에게 가하는 무언의 압박이다. peer pressure(또래 압력)보다 범위가 넓고 다소 분석적인 어조다. pressure to + 동사 형태로 자주 쓴다.
examples: There's a lot of societal pressure to get married by thirty in some places.
I felt societal pressure to look busy all the time.
Societal pressure can make people say yes when they mean no.

similar.example: He started smoking because of peer pressure.
She pushed back against social expectations about career choices.

expressions.quote: you'd probably get a few weird glances
expressions.nuance_ko: 말없이 흘끗 쳐다보는 반응으로 사회적 어색함이나 눈총을 표현한다. get a few funny looks와 비슷하다. 구어체이며 you'd 같은 가정 표현과 잘 어울린다.
examples: If you wear shorts to that meeting, you'll get a few weird glances.
I got some weird glances when I ordered tea at a coffee festival.
She got weird glances for bringing her own cutlery.

similar.example: We got funny looks for singing on the train.
His outfit raised a few eyebrows at the interview.

expressions.nuance_ko: 원래 별개였던 것이 큰 흐름에 딸려 들어가 같은 범주로 취급될 때 쓴다. 약간 아쉽거나 부정적인 어감이 있다. get swept up in(~에 휘말리다)과 함께 알아 두면 좋다.
examples: Good ideas sometimes get swept in with the bad ones when a team starts cutting things.
Quiet cafés got swept in with the new trend of co-working spaces.
I got swept up in the excitement and bought two tickets.

similar.example: Small shops got lumped in with big chains in the new rules.
I got caught up in the argument without meaning to.

expressions.quote: it got touted as this way to
expressions.nuance_ko: 누군가 열심히 밀어붙이듯 홍보한다는 뜻이고, 과장됐다는 회의적 뉘앙스를 풍기는 경우가 많다. be touted as the next big thing 같은 덩어리로 자주 쓴다. 뉴스와 토론에서 쓰기 좋다.
examples: That app is being touted as the next big thing, but I'm not convinced.
He's been touted as the future CEO for years.
The diet was touted as a miracle cure, which should've been a red flag.

similar.example: The film was hyped as the movie of the decade.
The event was billed as a casual get-together.

expressions.quote: almost pushback era of that content
expressions.nuance_ko: 새 정책이나 유행에 대한 반대 목소리를 말한다. get pushback from, push back against로 쓴다. 회의에서 'We got some pushback on the timeline.'처럼 매우 실용적인 표현이다.
examples: We got a lot of pushback from the team on the new schedule.
There's growing pushback against remote-work mandates.
I expected some pushback, but not this much.

similar.example: The decision caused a huge backlash online.
There was strong resistance to the plan.

expressions.quote: It's really up to the individual.
expressions.nuance_ko: 논쟁적인 주제에서 한발 물러나 존중하는 입장을 보일 때 쓴다. up to you/each person/the individual 형태로 바꿔 쓸 수 있다. 의견 표명을 피하는 느낌도 있어 토론에서는 근거를 덧붙이는 편이 좋다.
examples: Whether you work from home is really up to the individual.
I don't judge. How people spend their weekends is up to them.
It's up to the individual to decide how much risk they're comfortable with.

similar.example: Whether to have kids is a personal choice.
I'd never eat that, but to each their own.

expressions.quote: I think it's just all about balance, really.
expressions.nuance_ko: it's all about + 명사는 '핵심은 ~이다'라는 구어체 패턴이다. just와 really가 붙어 말투가 부드럽고 단정적이지 않다. 극단을 피하는 절충적 결론에 잘 쓴다.
examples: With work and family, it's all about balance, isn't it?
Investing is all about timing and patience.
I don't think there's one right way. It's just all about finding what works for you.

similar.example: I love cake, but everything in moderation.
In the end, it comes down to trust.

expressions.meaning_ko: 나는 그렇다고 말하기 어렵다 (나는 그렇지 않다)
expressions.nuance_ko: 상대 말에 가볍게 반대하거나 대비를 보일 때 쓴다. 뒤에 'I did...'처럼 자신의 경우를 이어 말하면 유머러스하다. 완전한 부정보다 부드러운 대비다.
examples: You slept eight hours? I can't say the same. The neighbours were loud.
She loved the hotel, but I can't say the same about the breakfast.
He's calm under pressure. I can't say the same for myself.

similar.expression: I wish I could say the same
similar.example: You finished early? I wish I could say the same.
It was great for them, not so much for me.

vocab.example: I'm staying sober tonight because I'm driving.
I learned to bake bread during lockdown.

vocab.meaning_ko: 자기 최적화, 자기계발 (생산성·건강 등을 끊임없이 개선하려는 경향)
vocab.example: Some people find all this self-optimisation exhausting.
A short walk at lunch keeps me sane on busy days.

vocab.meaning_ko: 브랜드 이미지에 어울리는, 광고주에게 부담 없는

vocab.example: I play tennis on a recreational basis, nothing serious.
Whilst I understand your point, I still disagree.
Half of my team are non-drinkers, so we pick cafés now.

warmup.q: Do you think drinking is a big part of social life in your country or workplace?
warmup.hint_ko: 회식 문화, 첫 잔 관례, 거절할 때의 분위기를 구체적 장면으로 설명해 보기.

warmup.q: Have you ever tried cutting down on something, like coffee, sugar or social media? How did it go?
warmup.hint_ko: 무엇을 줄였는지, 얼마나 지속했는지, 가장 어려웠던 점을 말하기.

opinion.q: Why do you think younger generations are drinking less than older ones?
opinion.hint_ko: 비용, 건강 인식, SNS와 기록 문화, 코로나 영향 같은 요인을 두세 개 골라 근거와 함께 설명.

opinion.q: Is the rise of self-optimisation content healthy, or does it just create new pressure?
opinion.hint_ko: 동기부여 효과와 비교·강박이라는 부작용을 비교하고, 본인 경험이나 주변 사례를 곁들이기.

debate.q: Should companies stop organising team events around alcohol?
debate.for: Alcohol-centred events exclude non-drinkers and create subtle pressure; inclusive events build better team bonds.
debate.against: Adults can decide for themselves; drinks help people relax and bond, and banning them feels paternalistic.

debate.q: Is the sober trend a lasting cultural shift or just another passing fad?
debate.for: Health awareness, cost and changing social habits point to a long-term change in norms.
debate.against: Trends swing back: the current pushback suggests people tire of lifestyle fads and return to old habits.

roleplay.scenario: A colleague's farewell dinner. You've decided not to drink for a few months, and a teammate keeps offering you drinks.
roleplay.your_role: A colleague who is cutting down on alcohol and wants to decline politely without making it awkward.
roleplay.partner_role: A friendly but pushy teammate who thinks everyone should drink at farewell dinners and questions your choice.
goals: Decline politely using expressions like 'step away from' and 'cut down on'.
Handle the pushback by saying 'it's up to the individual' without sounding preachy.
Close on a warm note, for example 'it's all about balance', and suggest another way to celebrate.

useful_phrases.phrase: I'm not going to give it away.
useful_phrases.ko: 그건 말 안 해 줄 거예요 (정답·비밀을 숨길 때).

useful_phrases.phrase: It was the norm back then.
I got some pushback on that.
It's really up to the individual.
I think it's all about balance, really.

shadowing.reason_ko: like, you know, 같은 군말과 you'd probably get 같은 가정 표현이 섞인 실제 구어체 문장이라 리듬과 연음 연습에 좋다.
개인 선택을 존중하면서 자기 입장을 밝히는 구조(I've decided... but I don't think...)를 그대로 쓸 수 있다.
'I think it's just all about balance, really.' 같은 부드러운 결론 표현과 자연스러운 대화 전환이 담겨 있다.

difficulty.note_ko: 느리고 또렷한 대본형 대화라 C1 학습자에게는 듣기 부담이 거의 없다. 대신 사회 현상 토론에 쓸 연결·완곡 표현(pushback, touted as, up to the individual 등)과 구어 패턴을 챙기는 용도로 적합하다. 학습자 수준의 B1~B2 청취용이나 쉬운 워밍업 자료로 추천한다.

translations.s2: 안녕하세요, 조지. 저한테는 꽤 특이한 얘기 하나 들어보실래요?
translations.s4: 저 올해는 술을 한 잔도 안 마셨어요.
translations.s5: 와! 정말 대단하네요. 기분이 어때요? 완전히 새사람이 된 것 같아요?
translations.s7: 저는 그렇다고 말은 못 하겠어요. 주말에 친구들이랑 술을 몇 잔 마셨거든요. 하지만 세계 여러 곳에서는 사람들이 아예 술을 안 마시기도 해요. 영국에서는 술 마시는 게 아주 흔했죠, 최근까지는요. 오늘 6 Minute English에서는 왜 많은 사람들이 술을 끊거나 줄이기로 하는지 알아보고, '이게 영국 음주 문화의 끝일까?'라는 질문을 던져 볼 거예요.
translations.s8: 좋아요. 닐, 퀴즈 문제부터 시작해 볼게요. 영국을 비롯한 여러 나라에서 많은 사람들이 새해에 1월 한 달 내내 술을 끊는데요, 이 도전을 뭐라고 부를까요? a) 새해 금주 b) 알코올 없는 1월, 아니면 c) 드라이 1월(Dry January)?
translations.s9: 음, 저는 답을 알지만 알려 주진 않을 거예요.
translations.s10: 좋아요. 그럼 청취자 여러분은 프로그램 끝에서 정답을 알게 되겠네요.
translations.s11: 네, 그렇죠. 그런데 조지, 요즘 젊은 사람들은 예전만큼 술을 안 마신다는 얘기를 항상 듣거든요. 그게 사실인가요?
translations.s12: 음, 영국의 조사에 따르면 16세에서 24세 사이는 윗세대보다 술을 안 마시는 사람일 가능성이 더 높다고 해요.
translations.s13: 그렇군요. 그럼 왜 더 많은 젊은 사람들이 맨정신으로 지내기로 하는 걸까요? 맨정신이라는 건 술을 마시지 않는다는 뜻이에요.
translations.s14: BBC World Service 팟캐스트 What in the World가 이걸 조사해 왔어요. 진행자 해나 겔바트가 무알코올 음료를 마시며 맨정신으로 지내기를 택한 젊은이 세 명을 만나 더 자세히 알아봤죠. 다니엘의 이야기를 들어 보세요.
translations.s15: 네. 지금은 술을 전혀 안 마시는데, 20대 초반에는 일종의 사회적 압박을 느꼈던 것 같아요. 회사 회식이나 대학 생활에서는 그냥 같이 마시는 게 당연했거든요. '난 아예 안 마실래요' 하면 이상하게 쳐다보는 눈길을 좀 받았을 거예요. 그래서 그렇게 지냈는데, 코로나 봉쇄 기간이 '좋아, 여기서 한 발 물러나 보자'라고 말할 용기를 조금 줬던 것 같아요.
translations.s16: 앞으로도 꼭 하고 싶은 일은 아니라는 생각이 들었죠.
translations.s17: 그럼 맨정신으로 지낸 지 몇 년째예요?
translations.s20: 다니엘은 어렸을 때 술을 마셔야 한다는 사회적 압박을 느꼈다고 말하네요. 사회적 압박이란 주변의 많은 사람들이 하고 있기 때문에 나도 해야 할 것 같다고 느끼는 걸 말해요.
translations.s21: 맞아요. 다니엘은 대학과 퇴근 후에는 술 마시는 게 당연했다고 하죠. the norm은 어떤 게 정상적이거나 흔하다는 걸 말하는 표현이에요.
translations.s22: 그런데 코로나19 팬데믹 동안 영국 사람들이 사람들과 어울리거나 펍과 바에 갈 수 없게 되자, 다니엘의 술에 대한 태도가 바뀌었어요. 그 후로 맨정신으로 지내기로 했고, 약 6년 동안 술을 마시지 않았죠.
translations.s23: 그러니까 조지, 많은 젊은 사람들이 술을 아예 안 마시고 그 경험을 소셜 미디어에 공유하는 것 같은데요. 그런데 최근에 약간 변화가 있었죠, 그렇죠?
translations.s24: 네. 많은 사람들이 술을 덜 마시거나 아예 안 마시는 경험을 소셜 미디어에 공유하는 한편, 어떤 사람들은 더 나가서 마시고 친구들과 즐겁게 놀고 싶다고 말하고 있어요. 우리가 건강과 웰빙을 너무 걱정한다고, 즐거운 시간을 위해 술을 좀 마시는 건 괜찮다고 주장하죠. 밀리가 BBC World Service 팟캐스트 What in the World에서 이에 대해 더 얘기하는 걸 들어 보세요.
translations.s25: 자기 최적화 콘텐츠가 급증한 시기가 있었다고 생각해요. 안타깝게도 금주도 그 흐름에 휩쓸려서, 새벽 5시에 일어나 하이록스를 하는 방법처럼 홍보됐죠. 그런데 우리 중 많은 사람들에게 술을 안 마시는 현실은 아마 그렇지 않아요. 좀 더 제정신으로 지내려고 하는 거죠, 뭐 그런 거요.
translations.s26: 그래서 지금은 그런 콘텐츠에 대한 일종의 반발 시대에 들어서고 있는 것 같아요. 술만 그런 게 아니라 담배 피우는 유명인들이 더 많이 보이고, 그걸 인스타그램에 올리면서 브랜드 이미지에 맞는지도 신경 쓰지 않죠.
translations.s27: 그렇군요. 밀리는 맨정신으로 지내는 게 특정 종류의 자기 최적화 콘텐츠와 연결되어 있다고 생각해요. 거기서는 사람들이 운동, 식단, 그리고 자신을 위한 큰 목표에 대해 얘기하죠.
translations.s28: 네, 그리고 밀리는 금주가 새벽 5시에 일어나 운동하는 방법으로 touted된다고 말해요. 다시 말해, 사람들이 그걸 많이 얘기하고 다른 사람들에게 하라고 부추긴다는 거죠.
translations.s29: 하지만 밀리는 맨정신으로 지내는 게 늘 엄청나게 건강하고 몸이 좋아지는 것만은 아니라고 말해요. 그녀에게는 제정신으로 지내는 것에 관한 거죠.
translations.s30: 그래도 밀리는 자기 최적화 콘텐츠에 대한 반발이 있다고 생각해요. pushback은 그 콘텐츠에 대한 비판을 뜻하고, 사람들은 정반대로 행동하면서 반발하고 있어요. 예를 들어 많은 유명인들이 자기가 술 마시고 담배 피우는 모습을 올리죠.
translations.s31: 음, 조지, 저는 1년 내내 술을 끊어 보기로 했는데, 원하지 않는다면 모두가 그럴 필요는 없다고 생각해요. 정말 개인에게 달린 문제죠.
translations.s32: 네, 저는 아직도 친구들과 술 몇 잔 마시는 게 좋아요. 결국 균형이 중요한 것 같아요. 자, 닐, 이번 주 질문의 답을 공개할 시간이에요. 제가 물었죠, '1월에 사람들이 술을 끊는 걸 뭐라고 부르나요?'
translations.s34: 맞아요. 잘했어요! 이번 프로그램에서 배운 어휘를 정리해 볼게요. 먼저 sober는 술이나 기분 전환용 약물을 하지 않는 사람을 묘사해요.
translations.s35: societal pressure는 다른 많은 사람들이 기대하기 때문에 내가 뭔가를 해야 한다고 느끼는 감정이에요.
translations.s36: 어떤 게 the norm이라고 말하는 건 그게 평소에 흔하다는 뜻이에요.
translations.s37: self-optimisation content는 건강하고 몸이 좋아지는 것, 그리고 큰 목표를 이루는 것에 관한 영상과 게시물을 뜻해요.
translations.s38: 누군가 어떤 생각이나 생활 방식을 tout한다면, 그것에 대해 많이 얘기하고 사람들에게 하라고 설득하려는 거예요.
translations.s39: 그리고 pushback은 어떤 유행에 대한 강한 비판, 그리고 정반대로 행동하는 사람들을 말해요.
translations.s40: 이번에도 6분이 다 지났네요. 하지만 웹사이트 bbclearningenglish.com의 워크시트로 배운 내용을 꼭 확인해 보세요.
